text:
B: Hiya. Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah, fine. I'm Kerry.
B: Gemma. Is this your first one?
A: First one, yeah. I was sat on my own last round. Have you done one already?
B: Just the one, with a woman called Claire. Lovely, talked a lot. So where are you?
A: Washington. Near Sunderland, not the American one.
B: I'd assumed. I'm Peterborough.
A: Right. Never been.
B: Not many people have, to be fair. It's got a cathedral and a lot of roundabouts. What do you do?
A: Team leader at a contact centre. Broadband and TV. I've got fourteen advisors and I take the escalations, so anyone who's really kicking off gets put through to me.
B: Do you get a lot of that?
A: Loads at the minute, with the price rises. People ring up shouting before you've said hello. You just let them get it out, to be honest. Most of them calm down once they've had their rant and they know you're actually going to sort it.
B: I'd be rubbish at that. I'd want to argue back.
A: Nah, you can't. What about you?
B: Quality engineer at an engine manufacturer. Parts come in, fail inspection, I find out why. Lots of spreadsheets and suppliers telling me it's not their fault.
A: Sounds like my job but with engines.
B: Ha, it probably is, to be fair. Someone's always blaming someone else.
A: That's every job, isn't it. I can't stand it when people make excuses instead of just saying they got it wrong.
B: Same. Just tell me what happened and we'll fix it, yeah?
A: Exactly. Is that a dog lead on your door in your photo? I clocked it.
B: Yeah, Pip, she's a lurcher. You had a dog bed in yours.
A: Tia. Staffy. She's eaten two settee cushions this year.
B: Pip ate a tea towel last week. Most of one.
A: Was she alright?
B: Fine. Came out the other end.
A: They're daft. Tia's soft as anything, though. People see a staffy and cross the road.
B: Do you get out with her much?
A: Most nights, round the wetland centre after work. That's my exercise, to be honest. Tried a gym once, bored stiff.
B: I do parkrun and five-a-side, but I'm a bit of a nutter about it. My partner thinks I'm mad.
A: What's his name?
B: Dean.
A: You're joking. Mine's Dean.
B: No way. What does yours do?
A: Plasterer. Self-employed.
B: Mine's a self-employed electrician. That's a bit weird, isn't it.
A: Bit, yeah. Has yours done that plaster behind you? That half-done bit in your photo?
B: No, that's me. I'm doing the spare room. Dean's useless with a hawk and trowel.
A: See, mine'd have that done in an afternoon. I'm doing ours up as well, really slowly. Been about two years.
B: Ha. Do you want kids, you two, or is it a spare spare room?
A: Erm... sorry, what d'you mean, like is it a nursery?
B: Yeah, sort of. Sorry, that's nosy.
A: Nah, you're alright. Just a spare room at the minute. Dean's keener than me, to be honest. We'll see.
B: Fair enough. We've mostly decided not to. My mum's not thrilled.
A: My mam'd be the same. She'd have it decorated for me.
B: Ha, mine drops hints over Sunday dinner.
A: We have Sunday tea at my mam's most weeks, so I get it with the roast potatoes.
